narrative.synopsis: Newborn Hermes refuses to remain a helpless infant. He steals Apollo’s cattle, hides the evidence, and then turns conflict into alliance by offering music Apollo cannot resist.
narrative.openingSituation: Hermes is newly born in Maia’s cave, apparently too young for divine mischief.
narrative.centralConflict: Apollo’s stolen cattle expose Hermes as a trickster before he has an official Olympian role.
narrative.resolution: Hermes’ lyre transforms accusation into exchange.
narrative.outcome: Apollo gains music, Hermes gains recognition, and trickery becomes part of divine order.

events.consequence: Hermes leaves the cradle on his birth day.
Apollo brings the theft before Zeus.
Hermes offers the lyre and wins reconciliation.
